Founders Friday · Pitchathon · 2026

iPrime

One app for money and movement in Katsina.

Wallet Bills Delivery Katsina State, Nigeria
Muhammad Umar Lawal — Founder
The problem

Ten million people, and not one app that serves them.

10.5M People in Katsina State — Nigeria's third most populous state.
51% Of adults in the North West are financially excluded, the highest rate in the country.
26M Nigerian adults still outside formal finance, concentrated in the North.

To send money, buy data and get a parcel across town, a Katsina resident needs a bank app built for Lagos, an agent who charges to move cash, and a phone call to a rider with no fixed price, no tracking and no recourse. Nigeria's delivery and fintech platforms stop at Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt.

Sources: EFInA Access to Finance survey; NBS / NPC state population projections.

The insight

Money and movement are the same problem.

Every errand in Katsina ends in a payment, and every payment is chasing something physical — a recharge, a meter token, a parcel, a plate of food.

Split those across separate apps and each one is too small to survive on its own in a secondary city. Put them on a single balance and every rail feeds the next: bills bring people back daily, delivery makes the balance worth keeping, and the balance makes delivery frictionless.

The wallet is not a feature. It is the distribution.

The product

One app. One balance. Three rails.

Rail 01 — Wallet

A real bank account, in ninety seconds.

Every user gets a Nigerian account number they can fund from any bank app. Send to any other user instantly, withdraw to any bank, authorise everything with a PIN. No BVN needed to get started.

Rail 02 — Bills

The reason they open it every day.

Airtime and data on all four networks, electricity tokens for every DISCO, cable and exam pins. Paid from the same balance, delivered instantly, automatically refunded if a purchase fails.

Rail 03 — Delivery

Food, groceries, pharmacy, parcels.

Priced by distance before you confirm. Broadcast to nearby riders, tracked live on a map, and paid automatically from the wallet the moment it is delivered.

How it works

Everything settles on one rail.

Money in Bank transfer User sends to their own iPrime account number from any bank app.
→
The rail Wallet balance One ledger. Every movement writes a transaction record against a balance snapshot.
→
Spend Bills · Delivery · Send Debited instantly, fulfilled in the background, refunded on failure.
→
Split Rider · Merchant · iPrime Settlement is automatic on completion. Nobody chases anybody for money.
→
Money out Withdraw to bank Riders and merchants cash out to any Nigerian bank, on demand.

Food, groceries, pharmacy and parcels all run through one request engine with one lifecycle, one tracking screen and one settlement path. Adding a category is a configuration change, not a rebuild.

Why now

Katsina decided to become a tech state. On the record.

FIRST

Katsina is the first state in Nigeria to domesticate the Nigeria Startup Act, establishing a State Council for Digital Innovation and Entrepreneurship.

₦250M

A guaranteed minimum annual allocation to the State Startup Grants and Investment Fund. Public capital is already committed to companies like this one.

$10BN

Katsina was selected by the Federal Government as one of ten states to host the national Innovation Hub programme.

145M

Active mobile lines nationally. In secondary cities, the smartphone is now the first financial device most people own, not the second.

Sources: Katsina State Digital Economy Policy; Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy; NCC subscriber data.

Status

This is not a concept. It is built and deployed.

4 Production surfaces: customer app, rider app, merchant dashboard, admin console.
300+ Live API endpoints across twenty backend modules.
44 Data models in a financial-grade PostgreSQL schema.
2 Apps submitted and sitting in Google Play closed testing.

Live web apps run at app.iprime.ng, so a first-time user can transact without installing anything. Rider location streams to the customer's map over WebSocket. Every wallet operation is a database transaction against a balance snapshot — no balance moves without a matching record.

Full disclosure: iPrime has not launched publicly. There are no customer numbers to show yet. Every figure from here on is a projection or a target, clearly marked as such.

How we make money

Four take rates, all of them already live in code.

Rail iPrime takes How it is charged Status
Delivery 30% Of a delivery fee set at ₦200 base plus ₦100 per kilometre. The rider keeps 70%. Implemented
Merchant orders 15% Commission on the basket, adjustable per merchant. The merchant keeps 85%. Implemented
Bills & airtime 2–4% Margin between wholesale VTU pricing and the retail price in the app. Implemented
Withdrawals Flat Per-payout fee when a user, rider or merchant cashes out to a bank. Implemented

Riders and merchants are paid automatically on completion, from the same balance the customer paid from. No invoicing, no float, no weekly reconciliation.

Go to market

Density first. One city, then the state, then the corridor.

Phase 1 — Months 0–6

Katsina metro

Sign 50 riders and 100 merchants along two commercial corridors. Bills build the daily habit and cost nothing to fulfil; delivery converts that habit into frequency and margin.

Phase 2 — Months 6–18

Daura, Funtua, Malumfashi

Same playbook on rails that already exist. A new town is a rider cohort and a merchant list, not an engineering project.

Phase 3 — Month 18+

The North West corridor

Kano, Kaduna, Zamfara. Every one of them has the same exclusion gap and the same absent incumbents.

Acquisition is physical, not digital: rider recruitment drives, merchant sign-up in the markets, and agent-assisted onboarding for first-time wallet users. That is exactly the work a Lagos platform will not do here.

The edge

Being local is the moat. Owning the stack is the leverage.

SUPPLY

The national platforms will not come to Katsina first. By the time they do, iPrime holds the rider supply, the merchant contracts and the wallet balances — the three things that take years, not money, to assemble.

OWNED

The source code, database and payment integrations are owned outright by the company. No licence fees, no vendor lock-in, no revenue share with a platform provider.

SPEED

Four verticals already run on one engine. Launching a fifth is a configuration change, while a competitor would be building a second product.

ACCESS

Founded and run from Katsina, with the merchant, rider and government relationships that cannot be bought from Lagos.

Appendix — Under the hood

Built to carry money, not just traffic.

LEDGER

Every wallet operation runs inside a database transaction against a balance snapshot. No balance moves without a matching transaction record.

QUEUES

Every third-party call — payments, airtime, notifications — goes through a job queue with retries. A failed utility purchase refunds automatically.

REALTIME

Rider location streams over WebSocket into a room scoped to a single request, so only the customer, the assigned rider and the merchant can see it.

LayerTechnology
Mobile appsReact Native (Expo), Android + iOS + web PWA
BackendNode.js, Express, 20 modules
DatabasePostgreSQL with Prisma, 44 models
RealtimeSocket.io
Queues & cacheBullMQ on Redis
PaymentsLicensed Nigerian provider: virtual accounts, payouts
BillsNational VTU aggregator
MapsGoogle Maps Platform
Appendix — What could go wrong

The four questions worth asking us.

RiskHow we handle it
Rider supply Riders keep 70% of every delivery fee and cash out on demand rather than waiting on a weekly payout. Recruitment starts before launch, not after.
Trust in a new wallet Funding happens by bank transfer to the user's own account number, so nobody hands cash to a stranger. Withdrawal is available from day one.
Regulation Wallet and payout rails run on a licensed Nigerian provider. iPrime holds no customer funds outside that provider.
A national platform arrives They arrive to a market where the riders, the merchants and the balances are already committed. Local density is the defence.
